sections.text: Identity and access management (IAM) is the enforcement point for the principle of least privilege. It answers two questions: who are you (authentication), and what are you allowed to do (authorization).

metadata.title: Identity and Access: OAuth 2.0, OIDC, RBAC, PAM, Service Accounts

sections.text:
```
IDENTITY AND ACCESS LANDSCAPE
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                                       |
|  AUTHENTICATION              AUTHORIZATION                            |
|  (who are you?)              (what can you do?)                       |
|  +-----------------------+   +---------------------------+            |
|  | Password + MFA        |   | RBAC (Role-Based)         |           |
|  | OAuth 2.0 flows       |   | ABAC (Attribute-Based)    |           |
|  | OIDC identity token   |   | ReBAC (Relationship-Based)|           |
|  | SAML 2.0 (legacy)     |   | Zanzibar (Google)         |           |
|  | Certificate-based     |   +---------------------------+           |
|  | WebAuthn / FIDO2          |                                       |
|  +-----------------------+   PRIVILEGED ACCESS                       |
|                               +---------------------------+           |
|  SERVICE IDENTITY             | PAM (Privileged Access    |           |
|  +-----------------------+   | Management)               |            |
|  | Managed identities    |   | JIT (Just-in-Time)        |           |
|  | Service principals    |   | Session recording         |           |
|  | Workload identity fed.|   | Credential vaulting       |           |
|  | Client credentials    |   +---------------------------+           |
|  +-----------------------+                                           |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
